land.text: Macedonia round Thessalonica and Thessaly to Domokos, Pharsalus and Velestino, formed from the partition of Byzantine lands in northern Greece with Thessaloniki as its capital (Kingdom page)

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Byzantine Empire (Angelos dynasty)'. Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1206; the page's founding year is 1204.

land.text: Thessalonica and the rest of the kingdom, taken by Theodore Komnenos Doukas in December 1224

successors.note: 'In 1224... Theodore finally captured Thessalonica and the kingdom became part of the Despotate of Epirus' (Kingdom page). The earlier Epirote gains (Larissa 1212, Platamon 1218, Serres 1221, the rest of Thessaly c.1222/3) are in the ledger.

land.text: Thessalonica, where Theodore 'soon after' declared himself emperor (Medieval Thessaly page)

successors.note: The infobox names the Empire of Thessalonica as the successor state; it is the same land as the Epirote hand-over above, one step later. Cliopatria's Empire of Thessalonica row begins in 1236.

capitals.name: Thessalonica (Thessaloniki)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Thessalonica'; the capital never moved in the life of the kingdom.

rulers.name: Boniface of Montferrat
rulers.title: King of Thessalonica
rulers.note: Infobox 'Boniface (1205-1207)'; the same page dates the kingdom from 1204. 'Boniface was killed in an ambush by the Vlach on 4 September 1207' (Boniface page).

rulers.name: Demetrius of Montferrat
rulers.title: King of Thessalonica (a child; regents: his mother Margaret of Hungary, then Eustace of Flanders from 1209/10)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Demetrius (1207-1224)'. Born at Thessalonica in 1205; crowned by Henry of Flanders on 6 January 1209 (Demetrius page); fled to Frederick II's court after 1224. His death is given as 1227 by the Theodore Komnenos Doukas page and as 1230 at Amalfi by the Demetrius page.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'Kingdom established: 1204' but Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1206. 'In 1204-05, Boniface was able to extend his rule south into Greece'; the Medieval Thessaly page has Boniface dividing Thessaly (Platamon to Rolando Piscia, Larissa and Halmyros to the Lombard Guglielmo, Velestino to Berthold of Katzenellenbogen), so the 1206 shape is drawn two years earlier. The page gives no area, so the infobox check could not be made; the ledger's 1205 vassal events cover the lordships south of the kingdom.

correction.text: the 1206 shape applied to 1204-1205: Macedonia round Thessalonica and Thessaly north of Domokos, Pharsalus and Velestino

keyframe_review.note: 33,017 km2 for 1206-1209; the Kingdom page gives no infobox area, so the shape cannot be checked against one (page silent). The Medieval Thessaly page says the boundaries 'seem to have extended only up to Domokos, Pharsalus, and Velestino' in southern Thessaly while the Spercheios valley (Zetounion, Ravennika) was under governors of the Latin emperor; the shape's southern edge (38.88N) touches only the Domokos plain, so it fits. The lordships south of it (Athens, Salona, Bodonitsa, Negroponte) were vassals to 1209 and are not in the shape.

The shape (33,116 km2) is right for 1210-1211 only. In 1212 Michael I of Epirus 'led his troops into Thessaly, overrunning the resistance of the local Lombard nobles', and 'Larissa and much of central Thessaly came under Epirote rule' (Medieval Thessaly); the Kingdom page adds that Michael attacked in 1210 and Henry defeated him. From 1212 use the _1212 keyframe.

correction.text: the 1210 shape unchanged for 1210-1211 (the years change, not the land)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1210 shape without Larissa and central Thessaly, which the Medieval Thessaly page gives to Epirus in 1212. The Larissa disc of 60 km is my reading of 'much of central Thessaly'; the remaining Thessalian lordships (Halmyros, the Pelion coast) went c.1222/3. The 1216 Cliopatria shape drops about 28 Thessalian cells and 12 more in western Macedonia (bbox 21.45-22.9E, 38.88-40.3N); the pages opened are silent on the western Macedonian part (Pieria, Elimeia), so it is kept here.

correction.text: the 1210 shape without Larissa and central Thessaly (Epirote from 1212)

keyframe_review.note: The shape (21,574 km2, bbox 22.10-25.64E, 39.385-41.39N) fits 1216-1217: Thessaly is gone except the Pelion coast and 'after initial reverses, much of Thessaly was conquered' by Epirus (Theodore page). Platamon still stands in it until its surrender in 1218, so the _1218 keyframe follows.

New keyframe: the 1216 shape without Platamon: 'culminating in the surrender of the great Platamon Castle in 1218' (Theodore page). Cliopatria's 1220 shape drops 19 cells (about 4,800 km2, bbox 22.12-22.93E, 39.44-40.85N), more than the castle's disc; the extra is the Pelion coast (c.1222/3) and Pieria, which the pages do not date.

correction.text: the 1216 shape without Platamon Castle at the Thermaic Gulf, surrendered to Theodore in 1218

keyframe_review.note: The shape (16,401 km2, 1220-1226) fits 1220-1221, Macedonia and Chalcidice with Thessalonica, but it runs two years past the kingdom: 'the exhausted defenders of Thessalonica surrendered the city to Theodore sometime in December 1224' (Theodore page; 'December 1224' also on the Demetrius page). It also keeps Serres, which surrendered in late 1221.

New keyframe: the 1220 shape without Serres: with 'the surrender of Serres in late 1221' Theodore cut the land link between Constantinople and Thessalonica (Theodore page). Held to December 1224; Chalcidice with Mount Athos fell 'already in 1224, or at least in 1225' and the east (Christopolis, Xanthi, Mosynopolis) in spring 1225, after the kingdom's end. The shape's eastern lobe (Kavala, to 25.5E) is Cliopatria's and may have been imperial rather than royal land (page silent).

region.text: Macedonia round Thessalonica, the capital: Boniface was given a large Macedonian territory with the title of king of Thessalonica (Baldwin page)

ledger.note: 1204: Boniface of Montferrat founds the Kingdom of Thessalonica at Thessalonica. Infobox 'Kingdom established: 1204'; the kingdom was formed from the partition of Byzantine lands in northern Greece; Baldwin I's page: 'in the summer of 1204, Baldwin came into collision with Boniface', and 'Boniface received Thessalonica as a fief from the emperor' (no month). The page gives the capital, not a boundary; the region is the 1206 shape without Thessaly.

region.text: Thessaly south of Mount Olympus as far as Domokos, Pharsalus and Velestino

ledger.note: 1204-05: Boniface takes Thessaly to the Domokos-Pharsalus-Velestino line. 'In 1204-05, Boniface was able to extend his rule south into Greece' (Kingdom page); Medieval Thessaly: Leo Sgouros gave up Thessaly without a fight after April 1204, and Boniface granted Platamon to Rolando Piscia, Larissa and Halmyros to the Lombard Guglielmo, Velestino to Berthold of Katzenellenbogen; the boundaries 'seem to have extended only up to Domokos, Pharsalus, and Velestino'. Year is the page's range 1204-05; counterpart is the empire's land, Sgouros being a local lord.

region.text: the Duchy (then Lordship) of Athens

ledger.note: 1205: the Lordship of Athens is a fief of the King of Thessalonica. The Kingdom page says the southern Greek principalities were Boniface's feudal vassals; the page dates Boniface's push south to 1204-05. The duchy dossier dates its own founding to 1205.

region.text: Euboea, the Triarchy of Negroponte

ledger.note: 1205: Euboea is held of the King of Thessalonica. Boniface of Montferrat, King of Thessalonica, received Euboea in the partition and granted it as a fief to Jacques II of Avesnes; in mid-1205 it passed to three Veronese barons (Triarchy of Negroponte page). The grant itself is undated on the page.

region.text: the Lordship of Salona (Amfissa)

ledger.note: 1205: the Lordship of Salona is a vassal of Boniface (Kingdom page: the southern Greek principalities were Boniface's feudal vassals). Medieval Thessaly: Salona went to Thomas d'Autremencourt. No dossier exists for Salona.

region.text: the Marquisate of Bodonitsa (Mendenitsa, by the Thermopylae pass)

ledger.note: 1205: the Marquisate of Bodonitsa is a vassal of Boniface (Kingdom page). Medieval Thessaly: Bodonitsa went to Guido Pallavicini. No dossier exists for Bodonitsa.

region.text: the Duchy (then Lordship) of Athens

ledger.note: 1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of duchy-of-athens on Thessalonica. In 1208-09 Emperor Henry campaigned against the rebellious Lombard barons and ended the feudal dependency of the Duchy of Athens, Bodonitsa, Salona and Negroponte, placing them under direct imperial suzerainty (Kingdom page, which gives the span 1208-09, not the month). Demetrius page: Henry 'advanced on Thessalonica in December 1208' and held the parliament at Ravennika.

region.text: Euboea, the Triarchy of Negroponte

ledger.note: 1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of the Triarchy of Negroponte on Thessalonica. In 1208-09 Emperor Henry campaigned against the rebellious Lombard barons and ended the feudal dependency of these four, placing them under direct imperial suzerainty (Kingdom page; the page gives the span, not the month). The Triarchy page has Ravano's homage to the Latin emperor in May 1209.

region.text: the Lordship of Salona (Amfissa)

ledger.note: 1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of Lordship of Salona on Thessalonica. In 1208-09 Emperor Henry campaigned against the rebellious Lombard barons and ended the feudal dependency of the Duchy of Athens, Bodonitsa, Salona and Negroponte, placing them under direct imperial suzerainty (Kingdom page, which gives the span 1208-09, not the month). Demetrius page: Henry 'advanced on Thessalonica in December 1208' and held the parliament at Ravennika.

region.text: the Marquisate of Bodonitsa (Mendenitsa, by the Thermopylae pass)

ledger.note: 1209: Henry of Flanders ends the feudal dependency of Marquisate of Bodonitsa on Thessalonica. In 1208-09 Emperor Henry campaigned against the rebellious Lombard barons and ended the feudal dependency of the Duchy of Athens, Bodonitsa, Salona and Negroponte, placing them under direct imperial suzerainty (Kingdom page, which gives the span 1208-09, not the month). Demetrius page: Henry 'advanced on Thessalonica in December 1208' and held the parliament at Ravennika.

region.text: the Thessaly that the Lombard lords still held after Larissa and central Thessaly passed to Epirus in 1212

ledger.note: 1212: Epirus invades Thessaly. Michael I of Epirus 'led his troops into Thessaly, overrunning the resistance of the local Lombard nobles' (Medieval Thessaly, section on 1212). The Kingdom page has Michael attacking Thessalonica itself in 1210 and being beaten by Henry, so 1212 is the first ground taken. The zone is the Thessaly left after Larissa; it is contested until Theodore finishes the region c.1222/3.

region.text: 'Larissa and much of central Thessaly'

ledger.note: 1212: Larissa and central Thessaly pass to Epirus. 'Larissa and much of central Thessaly came under Epirote rule' (Medieval Thessaly), which separated Thessalonica from the Crusader principalities in southern Greece. The Larissa disc of 60 km is my reading of 'much of central Thessaly'; mirrors despotate-of-epirus /ledger 1 (gain).

region.text: Macedonia from Pieria and the Thermaic Gulf to the Nestos: Platamon, Thessalonica, Serres, Chalcidice

ledger.note: 1218: Epirus presses into Macedonia. Platamon's surrender in 1218 is the first ground taken there; the siege of Thessalonica itself began only 'in early 1223' (Theodore page). The zone is Macedonia as the kingdom held it in 1216; it is contested until the fall of Thessalonica.

region.text: 'the great Platamon Castle', commanding the Thermaic Gulf

ledger.note: 1218: Platamon Castle surrenders to Theodore Komnenos Doukas. 'Culminating in the surrender of the great Platamon Castle in 1218.' The Medieval Thessaly page gives Platamon to Rolando Piscia in 1204-05; mirrors despotate-of-epirus /ledger 6.

region.text: Serres

ledger.note: Late 1221: Serres surrenders, cutting the road between Constantinople and Thessalonica. With 'the surrender of Serres in late 1221' Theodore cut the land link between Constantinople and Thessalonica (Theodore page). The page does not say whether Serres then belonged to King Demetrius or to the Latin emperor (the Demetrius page has Henry taking Serres from Lombard garrisons), so the year is the page's and the holder my reading.

region.text: 'the entire region except for Halmyros'

ledger.note: c. 1222/3: the rest of Thessaly passes to Epirus. By then Theodore 'completed the recovery of the entire region except for Halmyros, which remained in Latin hands until 1246' (Medieval Thessaly); the year is approximate (1222 chosen, matching despotate-of-epirus /ledger 8). Halmyros is a 12 km disc.

region.text: the Thessaly that the Lombard lords still held after Larissa and central Thessaly passed to Epirus in 1212

ledger.note: c. 1222/3: the Thessalian fighting ends with Epirus holding the region except Halmyros (Medieval Thessaly).

region.text: Thessalonica, 'Chalcidice with Mount Athos' and the Macedonian rest of the kingdom

ledger.note: December 1224: Thessalonica falls. 'The exhausted defenders of Thessalonica surrendered the city to Theodore sometime in December 1224' (Theodore page; 'Theodore forced the surrender of the city in December 1224', Demetrius page). 'Already in 1224, or at least in 1225, Theodore captured Chalcidice with Mount Athos'; the eastern lands (Christopolis, Xanthi, Mosynopolis) followed in spring 1225. Mirrors despotate-of-epirus /ledger 9.

region.text: Macedonia from Pieria and the Thermaic Gulf to the Nestos: Platamon, Thessalonica, Serres, Chalcidice

ledger.note: December 1224: the war for Macedonia ends with Thessalonica's surrender; Demetrius flees to Frederick II's court (Demetrius page).

region.text: the whole kingdom

ledger.note: December 1224: the Kingdom of Thessalonica falls to Epirus. Infobox 'Fall of Thessalonica to Epirus: 1224'; 'In 1224... Theodore finally captured Thessalonica and the kingdom became part of the Despotate of Epirus.' Theodore declares himself emperor soon after (Medieval Thessaly), founding the Empire of Thessalonica. Cliopatria's shape runs to 1226, two years late.

wars.name: Bulgarian war of Kaloyan against the Latins (Kingdom of Thessalonica's share)
wars.outcome: Boniface of Montferrat was ambushed and killed by the Bulgarians on 4 September 1207 and his head was sent to Tsar Kaloyan; the Kingdom page records no change of the kingdom's borders.
wars.note: Baldwin I's page: the Greeks of Thrace revolted in February 1205 relying on Kaloyan and the Franks were beaten at Adrianople on 14 April 1205. Cliopatria lists Bulgaria as a neighbour of the kingdom for 1206-1219; no page opened dates a frontier. Boniface page: 'killed in an ambush by the Vlach on 4 September 1207'.

wars.name: Lombard rebellion against Henry of Flanders
wars.outcome: Henry advanced on Thessalonica in December 1208, crowned the child Demetrius on 6 January 1209 'extracting oaths of homage from the Lombard barons', and held a parliament at Ravennika; the feudal dependency of Athens, Bodonitsa, Salona and Negroponte on Thessalonica ended.
wars.note: Kingdom page: Henry marched against the regency in 1209 and forced its submission and his brother Eustace became regent. No land changed hands inside the kingdom.

wars.name: Epirote conquest of the Kingdom of Thessalonica

zones.text: the Thessaly that the Lombard lords still held after Larissa and central Thessaly passed to Epirus in 1212
Macedonia from Pieria and the Thermaic Gulf to the Nestos: Platamon, Thessalonica, Serres, Chalcidice

wars.outcome: Michael I of Epirus attacked in 1210 and was beaten by Henry; he took Larissa and central Thessaly in 1212; Theodore took Platamon (1218), Serres (late 1221), the rest of Thessaly except Halmyros (c.1222/3), besieged Thessalonica from early 1223 and took it in December 1224.
wars.note: Kingdom page: over nine years Theodore gradually conquered all of the kingdom except the city of Thessalonica, because the Latin Empire was fighting the Empire of Nicaea in Asia. Relief expeditions: a Latin army sent against Serres in April 1224 was destroyed; a crusader force landed at Halmyros in March 1225, after the fall.

certainty.note: A feudal kingdom of fiefs whose edges the pages give only by towns: 'up to Domokos, Pharsalus, and Velestino' in the south; the eastern edge (Nestos) and the western Macedonian edge are Cliopatria's. The coast and the Thermaic Gulf are exact.

notes: Pages opened: six for this state (budget five) plus the Triarchy of Negroponte page, opened for the negroponte dossier and cited for Euboea. Cliopatria row: 'Kingdom of Thessalonica' 1206-1226 starts two years after the 1204 founding and ends two years after the December 1224 fall (the 1220 shape runs to 1226); corrections are the _1204 and _1222 keyframes and the 1224 dissolve. The Kingdom page gives no infobox area (page silent), so the area check could not be made; shapes are 33,017 / 33,116 / 21,574 / 16,401 km2. Not settled: (1) the month of the founding (Baldwin's page: summer 1204 quarrel, no date for the agreement; the latin-empire dossier dates the vassalage to October 1204 and an agreement of 16 May 1204, neither of which the Kingdom page contains); (2) the western Macedonian loss between the 1210 and 1216 shapes (12 cells, bbox 21.45-22.9E, 38.88-40.3N outside Thessaly) and the Pieria loss between the 1216 and 1220 shapes, which no page opened dates; (3) whether the eastern lobe of the 1220 shape (Kavala, to 25.5E) was royal or imperial land; (4) Demetrius's death (1227 on the Theodore page, 1230 at Amalfi on the Demetrius page); (5) Halmyros stayed 'in Latin hands until 1246' after the kingdom's fall and is in no successor's land. The Duchy of Athens, Lordship of Salona, Marquisate of Bodonitsa and Negroponte are drawn as Thessalonican vassals 1205-1209 (vassal events); Salona and Bodonitsa have no dossier or Cliopatria row. The kingdom itself was a vassal of the Latin Empire (infobox 'Vassal of the Latin Empire'); the latin-empire dossier carries that relation (vassal_start 1204, vassal_end 1224). Family 'italy' (Montferrat, Lombard barons) is a key of colours.json; the sibling dossiers use 'latin', which is not. Region names the gazetteer lacks: Karystos is not used here; Salona/Amfissa and Bodonitsa/Mendenitsa are radii around coordinates.
